summary:
Radar for 2026-11-14, GLP-1 focus. Four things stand out this week.

1. **Stopping and keeping results.** Several mainstream outlets covered it in the last 48 hours: Medscape, Fox, Yahoo "I hit my goal weight, what now?", and Medical Daily on an unreviewed regain analysis. That refreshes our best broad Lane A topic, which already has proof (Stopping: 7.78% CTR).
2. **Thanksgiving.** Fullness and nausea Shorts start Nov 18. Search peaks Nov 18–27.
3. **Gene variants (emerging, low competition).** Two Nature Metabolism papers (13 Nov) found that people with rare damaging GLP1R gene variants lost much less weight on semaglutide (2.4% vs 8.8% in matched non-carriers). Their weight loss on tirzepatide was near-normal (13.3% vs 15.2%). This answers the common question "why didn't my GLP-1 work?" It is genetic cohort data, not a randomized trial.
4. **ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov).** The full REDEFINE 4 data (CagriSema vs tirzepatide, 809 adults, 84 weeks; 23.0% vs 25.5%, non-inferiority not met) may be presented. It is the only possible EloraTZP-style fast-turn. The topline came out months ago and evergreen CagriSema videos flopped, so only make it if a new full publication drops.

**Search-demand formats to keep running:**
- first-month what-to-expect timeline
- pen and injection-site how-to (IFU only)
- the NAION label change explained with the absolute risk
- felt symptoms: nausea, hair loss, burping, injection site

**Use with caution:**
- psychiatric symptoms after stopping: only 2 published case reports, picked up by tabloids
- the Danish study of 750,000 pregnancies (Human Reproduction Open): diabetes-specific preterm signal, observational

**Rejected:**
- compounded, research-use and black-market sourcing stories (the Utah additive study, the Join Luma price PR)
- cost and coverage news: CVS $350, Deloitte, the Wegovy pill price

**Long-form ruled out by our own data, even with fresh research:**
- narrow single-symptom topics
- pipeline explainers
- single-trial deep dives

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) after you stop: what SURMOUNT-4 shows about keeping results (335 vs 335 randomized; +14.0% regain on placebo from week 36 to 88, placebo group still 9.9% below starting weight), refreshed by this week's 'what happens when you stop' coverage
candidates.angle: Broad Lane A long-form: 'You hit your goal. Now what?' Explain what the trial showed (regain on average, and a big range between people). Then cover the habits the evidence supports: protein, strength training and an ongoing prescriber plan. No stopping or tapering advice. Our Stopping long-form already exists, so make this the follow-up on keeping results, linked from Stopping and EloraTZP.
keywords: what happens when you stop mounjaro
how to keep weight off after tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: ongoing; news spike 3–10 days, then evergreen through January resolutions
candidates.why_now: Five outlets covered stopping GLP-1s in 48 h: Medscape, Fox News, Yahoo Health, Medical Daily and a Lancet Regional Health Europe records study. It fits our proven broad-question rule (Stopping: 7.78% CTR, 288 min by day 9). The New Year restart season begins in about 6 weeks.

I hit my goal weight on a GLP-1, what now? (13 Nov)
Ozempic and Zepbound users face 6 rebound risks after stopping (12 Nov)
SURMOUNT-4 record (randomized withdrawal design)

candidates.topic: Why a GLP-1 can work less for some people: rare GLP1R gene variants cut semaglutide weight loss (2.4% vs 8.8% in matched non-carriers), but carriers responded near-normally to tirzepatide (13.3% vs 15.2%) (Nature Metabolism, 13 Nov)
candidates.angle: Calm, non-blaming Short for 'my medicine isn't working': for a small group of people, biology may be part of the answer. Explain why: semaglutide works on one receptor, while tirzepatide works on two (GLP-1 and GIP). This is genetic cohort data from 13,725 treated adults, not a randomized trial and not a test you can order. End with 'bring it up with your prescriber', never 'switch'. It can also be a chapter in a broad 'Tirzepatide not working?' long-form.
keywords: why isn't ozempic working for me
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days as science press and creators pick it up
candidates.why_now: Two Nature Metabolism papers came out on 13 Nov, and only Bioengineer and science trade press have covered them so far. Science American-level coverage is plausible. Few creators have it yet, and the 'not working' search intent is large and evergreen.

evidence.signal: Rare GLP1R variants attenuate weight loss with semaglutide but not tirzepatide (13,725 GLP-1RA-treated adults)
Companion paper: Rare GLP1R variants diminish the weight loss effect of semaglutide but not of tirzepatide
23andMe study of 27,885 users: common variants have modest effects; a GIPR variant is linked to tirzepatide nausea

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full after a few bites, protein first, smaller plates, eating slowly, and easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: 'Is this normal?' Short: full after 3 bites at Thanksgiving. This is a felt moment, and it was our best Reel (428 views). Point to the What to Eat and Thanksgiving long-forms. Post from Nov 18, not before, because posting too early flopped.
keywords: full after a few bites zepbound
how to eat thanksgiving on GLP-1
candidates.why_now: The seasonal search peak starts in 4 days. It has appeared in 9 snapshots at 88–93 momentum. The playbook schedules holiday-fullness Shorts from Nov 18.

evidence.signal: GI adverse reactions occurred mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time
Holiday 'full after 3 bites' Reel: 428 views, our best Reel

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) first month: what to expect week by week (appetite, food noise, GI effects mostly during dose escalation, injection-site reactions), from the label and SURMOUNT trials
candidates.angle: What-to-expect timeline long-form, one of the search-demand formats. Open with 'You just did your first shot.' Use label wording for side-effect timing, include no dosing or titration steps, and add questions to ask your prescriber. Link it to Side Effects.
candidates.why_now: New starts are rising. The first-month video is scheduled for its day-7 check on 11-20, so a follow-up piece (a months 2–3 timeline) is the next in the priority order. It's a proven search-demand format.

evidence.signal: Adverse reaction rates by dose and timing language
Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects (13 Nov)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) side effects: foods and habits that may ease nausea, constipation, diarrhea and reflux (smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping when full, less greasy food, fluids)
candidates.angle: Broad long-form next in the priority order ('foods that ease side effects'). The narrow symptoms become chapters, not separate videos. Re-hook at each symptom chapter, and use the label's dehydration and kidney caution as the safety beat.
keywords: what to eat on mounjaro to avoid nausea
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; boosted by holiday meals Nov 18–Jan 1
candidates.why_now: CNN's 'Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects' (13 Nov) is mainstream pickup. Side Effects is our internal hub (1,064 min), and the narrow-symptom videos underperform as standalone long-forms.

evidence.signal: Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects
GI adverse reactions; acute kidney injury warning linked to dehydration

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the FDA's NAION eye warning, label change explained: absolute risk (6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years across 126 RCTs) and the sudden-vision-loss symptoms that need same-day care
candidates.angle: Label-change long-form (a search-demand format): what changed on the label, what NAION is, the absolute numbers, and which symptoms need urgent care. No 'quit now' framing. The differentiator is the calm absolute risk. Cite the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) explainer and NANOS.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–5 days for news; label-change search lingers 4–8 weeks
candidates.why_now: The AAO, MedPage, NeurologyLive, The Hill and local TV have all covered it in the last 72 h. The Hill op-ed's fear framing creates demand for a calm explainer. Shorts on label news underperformed (48 views), so make this a long-form only.

evidence.signal: Here's what you need to know about the FDA's new GLP-1 warning (11 Nov)
FDA requires NAION warning across GLP-1 RA class (13 Nov)
What was FDA's GLP-1 warning about? (13 Nov)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection: pen how-to and injection-site rotation per the Instructions for Use, plus what's normal (redness, itching; 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo)
candidates.angle: Device how-to plus a 'Is this normal?' Short pair: the IFU steps only, with no amounts. Visible-body worries are our proven Short winners (242 and 188 views). Point the Short to Side Effects with a related-video link.
candidates.why_now: This search-demand format beat channel averages by 10–195x in the niche. The pen how-to's day-7 read is on 11-18. Injection-site Shorts are our second-best Short theme.

evidence.signal: Injection-site reactions by dose vs placebo
Pen steps and injection areas (IFU)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide nausea at holiday meals: why it happens, why it's usually worst during dose escalation, and what helps
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom Short ('tirzepatide nausea' is a top typed search) tied to the holidays: smaller plates, stop at the first sign of fullness, less greasy food. Include the label's 'mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time' line and when to call your prescriber (vomiting with dehydration signs).
candidates.why_now: Nausea Shorts reached 180 views (above our median). Holiday meals bring the symptom back, and a GIPR variant tied to tirzepatide nausea gives the Short one new fact.

evidence.signal: Nausea rates by dose; GI effects mostly during escalation
GIPR variant associated with nausea only on tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol at holiday parties: what the label says, no 'safe amount', and the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas
candidates.angle: Answer the holiday-party question. Cover what the evidence and label say, keep the GI and dehydration overlap clear, and treat the DOM target trial emulation (type 2 diabetes, observational) as a 'linked to' fact only.
candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 5 snapshots. Party season starts in about 2 weeks, and the playbook lists it as a Lane A topic.

evidence.signal: Systematic review: incretin therapies for alcohol use disorder
GLP-1R activation in the thalamus suppresses alcohol responses (animal study, mechanism only)

candidates.topic: Strength training on tirzepatide: the T-REx randomized trial (Nature Medicine, 9 Nov). Resistance exercise for 40 weeks cut lean-mass loss by about 25% vs usual activity in 120 adults with overweight or obesity
candidates.angle: Use it as the fresh fact in a 'Will I lose muscle on tirzepatide?' felt-worry Short, and as a chapter update in the Strength long-form. Don't make a single-trial deep dive.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical (12 Nov), MindBodyGreen and Korean press picked it up, and the Lancet COURAGE muscle-drug trial adds to the muscle conversation. Creators are only starting to cover it.

evidence.signal: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy: RCT
Muscle benefits of lifting weights while taking tirzepatide (12 Nov)

candidates.topic: CagriSema vs tirzepatide, REDEFINE 4 full data at ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov): open-label, 84 weeks, 809 adults with obesity plus at least one comorbidity; 23.0% vs 25.5% (efficacy estimand), non-inferiority not met
candidates.angle: Make this only if a full publication or new data drops at ObesityWeek within 48 h. Then do a fast-turn 'Did CagriSema beat tirzepatide?' extra L2 on the EloraTZP model, or the 13:00 tirzepatide-first head-to-head Short. Say clearly that CagriSema isn't approved and the trial was open-label.
candidates.why_now: It is the only randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide possibly going public this week. The topline came out months ago, though, and our evergreen CagriSema video flopped (117 min). Verify that there is new full data before making anything.

evidence.signal: CagriSema fails primary non-inferiority endpoint vs tirzepatide
REDEFINE 4 results vs tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: what the label reports (5.4% vs 0.9%; women 7.1%, men 0.5%) and why rapid weight loss is a known link
candidates.angle: The one hair Short allowed this week, only once the Hair long-form is verified clean. New angle: why women report it more in the label data. Don't repeat the 'grow back' angle.
candidates.why_now: Our best Short theme (1,025 views). People keep searching this felt symptom.

evidence.signal: Hair loss 5.4% vs 0.9% placebo, sex breakdown

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) what to expect, label only: the approved GLP-1 pill, plus China approval (12 Nov) and the ATTAIN-OSA sleep apnea results
candidates.angle: What-to-expect long-form for an approved drug with search demand ('foundayo' brought 19 searches, 332 min). Use the label's top dose (17.2 mg) and Trial 1 at −11.1%. The China news and the sleep apnea data are context only.
candidates.why_now: Reuters and wire coverage of the China approval are boosting brand-name searches. The sleep apnea Phase 3 came out at AHA. It's in the priority order.

evidence.signal: Eli Lilly first with a GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved in China (12 Nov)
Has Foundayo found its niche in sleep apnoea? (12 Nov)

candidates.topic: Mood changes after stopping tirzepatide: what's confirmed? Two published case reports (Primary Care Companion for CNS Disorders) of psychiatric symptoms weeks after stopping, now amplified by the NY Post and NewsNation
candidates.angle: Calm 'what's confirmed' Short. It's 2 case reports, which can't show cause or how common it is. The FDA removed the 'Suicidal Behavior and Ideation' class warning, which is a separate issue. Any mood change while on the medicine or after stopping is worth raising with your prescriber, and give the crisis line for all four markets. No fear framing, no stopping advice.
candidates.why_now: The NY Post, NewsNation, Health and Me and several aggregators covered it on 11–14 Nov, so the tabloid curve is still climbing. There's high risk of misinformation from other creators, and a calm, accurate version is scarce.

evidence.signal: Why are patients reporting mania, hallucinations after stopping Ozempic? (14 Nov)
FDA requests removal of the Suicidal Behavior and Ideation warning from GLP-1 RA labels
Some GLP-1 patients suffer psychosis after stopping, reports say

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide burping and heartburn: sulfur burps and reflux after big meals, and what helps
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom Short ahead of the holiday meals. Don't say slower emptying 'causes' it; say the label describes delayed gastric emptying and lists eructation and GERD as reactions. Practical tips, plus when to call your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 10 snapshots combined, and holiday meals bring it back. The earlier heartburn Short is still too young to judge (31 views).

evidence.signal: Eructation, dyspepsia and GERD listed as adverse reactions

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the kidneys: new parent-trial-level meta-analysis on albuminuria, eGFR and kidney outcomes (Diabetes Res Clin Pract, 13 Nov)
candidates.angle: 'Benefits beyond weight' Short or a chapter. Keep it to what the trials measured (mostly albuminuria and eGFR markers in SURPASS and SURMOUNT populations). Make clear that tirzepatide has no kidney indication, and contrast it with semaglutide's FLOW result in its own population.
candidates.why_now: It's fresh, with no press pickup yet. Our audience overlaps with people who have type 2 diabetes and CKD, and the 'Medical Republic' piece on semaglutide and CKD shows clinician interest.

evidence.signal: Kidney effects of tirzepatide: systematic review and meta-analysis (13 Nov)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines around pregnancy: Danish study of 750,000 pregnancies (Human Reproduction Open). No preterm signal for weight-loss use; higher preterm risk among women with pre-existing diabetes
candidates.angle: Only as a 'what's confirmed' Short. It's observational, the signal is in the diabetes group and may reflect the diabetes itself, and the labels still say to stop before a planned pregnancy on a prescriber's advice. Pair it with the tirzepatide birth control label line. Low priority: birth control content flopped.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily (13 Nov), SciTechDaily and Live Science are covering it, with conflicting headlines. The 'Ozempic baby' thread from NPR is continuing.

evidence.signal: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
Study links GLP-1 use to some pregnancy risks, with key caveats

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain: TRIUMPH-4 phase 3 (WOMAC pain −4.0 at 9 mg, −3.7 at 12 mg vs −2.1 placebo at 68 weeks)
candidates.angle: Only a 13:00 'what's confirmed' Short with Phase 3 data (retatrutide Phase 3 Shorts got 84–280 views). Say clearly that it isn't approved, and give no sourcing information.
candidates.why_now: The Washington Post, Medical News Today and Medical Republic have all covered it. It's past the early window, and Rogan's mention adds hype, plus gray-market risk.

evidence.signal: 2 trials link new weight-loss drug to knee pain relief (11 Nov)

candidates.topic: REJECT: compounded, research-use and black-market GLP-1 sourcing stories (University of Utah study on untested additive combinations, Join Luma 'cheapest compounded' press release, BBC black-market jab story, 'retatrutide peptide research' resource listicles) and cost or coverage news (CVS $350, Deloitte coverage cut, Wegovy pill price)
candidates.angle: Don't make content that names sellers, prices or sourcing routes. At most one gray-market warning Short a week, framed as 'research vials aren't the medicine'. Cost and coverage are banned topics.
candidates.why_now: There is a lot of news volume, but brand rules forbid sourcing promotion and the playbook bans cost and Medicare angles.
